newsitem.title: USA: Orange Cty's Citron may qualify for work program.
newsitem.headline: Orange Cty's Citron may qualify for work program.

text.p: Former Orange County, Calif., Treasurer Robert Citron may qualify for a community work program in lieu of serving time in jail for his role in the county bankruptcy crisis, authorities said Tuesday.
The Orange County sheriff's department was expected to determine whether Citron qualifies for the program in January, said Lt. Tom Garner, a spokesman for the sheriff's department.
"We won't know until he gets here," said Garner. "We'll look at his physical and mental person and would then make a determination."
Garner said the community work program was generally designed for first-time and non-violent offenders. About 375 people are currently in the work program in Orange County.
If Citron qualifies for the program, he would be assigned a job in the county instead of serving a year in county jail.
Orange County filed for bankruptcy protection on Dec. 6, 1994, after sustaining losses of more than $1.6 billion on risky investments. The county emerged from bankruptcy in June.
In November, a judge ordered Citron to spend a year in jail and pay a $100,000 fine for his role in the investment crisis.
Citron was ordered to report to jail on January 10.
But neither the prosecution nor the defense said they expected Citron to serve a full year in jail.
The district attorney's office said in November that Citron was likely to serve only nine months in custody of the year term, provided he receive credit for good behavior.
Citron's attorney said he hoped Citron would qualify for home confinement instead of jail time.
Citron pleaded guilty in April 1995 to six felonies, including counts of making untrue statements in the sale of securities and misusing public funds.
